top_story: The Houthi seizure of Mocha on 10 September appears to have accelerated their push along Yemen’s Red Sea coast, and by 12 September the offensive had reopened broader fighting that caused more than 900 casualties and drove at least 5,000 families from their homes. As the advance neared the Bab al-Mandab corridor, displacement surged to nearly 50,000 civilians, showing how a military contest over ports and shipping access is rapidly becoming a mass protection crisis for coastal communities. In Lebanon, the 9 September killing of 12 members of one family, including six children, underscored that Israeli strikes continue to hollow out the meaning of ceasefire diplomacy for civilians. The regional picture is one of active front lines overriding de-escalation efforts, with chokepoint competition and recurrent strikes deepening public insecurity far beyond the battlefield.
